subject: Linguistics
title: Language and Social Class
description: Learn Language and Social Class in one minute.

hook.text: In a BBC interview, accent alone can signal whether someone went to Eton or a state school.

buildup.text: Basil Bernstein proposed that social class affects not just accent but entire communication styles.

discovery.text: Working-class speech tends to use more local features; middle-class speech aligns toward the standard.

twist.text: Lower-middle-class speakers often 'hypercorrect'—using prestige forms even more than upper-class speakers.

climax.text: Class differences in language reinforce social boundaries—accent becomes a gatekeeping mechanism.

punchline.text: Your voice can open doors—or close them.

quiz.question: What is hypercorrection?
options: Using prestige forms more than upper-class speakers do
